questions.name: Collection Protocol Clarity
questions.description: Description completeness of participant recruitment and data acquisition
questions.score_label: Full recruitment and procedural details included
questions.evidence: Collection mechanisms (lines 355-373): Voice data collected in clinic using custom Bridge2AI-Voice App on iPad (9th or 10th generation) or iPad Air (5th generation) with Avid AE-36 microphone and Apple dongle connector, research assistant present. Acquisition methods (lines 375-404): 22 acoustic tasks for adults detailed (Respiration, Cough, Prolonged Vowel, Rainbow Passage, Free Speech, etc.), 36 pediatric tasks listed, validated questionnaires (VHI-10, PHQ-9, GAD-7, MOCA, etc.), EHR access for consenting participants. Recruitment (lines 274-299): Non-probability purposive sampling from high volume expert specialty clinics (>50 patients/month), screening per inclusion/exclusion criteria (protocol Table 1), English-speaking adults 18-120 years. Data collectors (lines 407-414): Research teams at 5 North American sites, medical/graduate/undergraduate students with site clinicians, participant compensation ($40/<90min, $80/>90min, max $120). Timeframes (lines 416-422): September 2022 through November 2026, version-specific release dates
questions.quality_note: Exceptional collection protocol clarity with complete procedural details. Hardware specifications (iPad models, microphone model), software (Bridge2AI-Voice App), all acoustic tasks enumerated, questionnaire instruments named, recruitment strategy detailed (specialty clinic criteria), inclusion/exclusion referenced, data collector roles defined, compensation structure provided, timeline documented. Meets highest standard for reproducibility and transparency.

questions.name: Human Subject Representation

questions.evidence: Instance description (lines 221-240): 833 adult participants, 300 pediatric participants, recruited from specialty clinics across North America, five predetermined disease cohort groups, diagnostic labels by clinical assessment (laryngoscopy, stroboscopy, MRI, CT, genome sequencing, EHR, medication). questions.name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
questions.description: Describes how users can obtain the dataset
questions.score_label: Fully defined access path (platform, login, policy)
questions.evidence: Two-tier access mechanism fully documented: (1) Registered Access (lines 244-254, 573-585): featurized dataset distributed through PhysioNet (https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/), requires PhysioNet account and signed Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement (DUA), includes spectrograms, MFCCs, OpenSMILE features, phenotype data, HIPAA Safe Harbor deidentified. (2) Controlled Access (lines 256-263): raw audio waveforms require separate application via DACO@b2ai-voice.org, Data Access Request Form (DARF), Data Use Agreement (DUA), institutional Data Use and Transfer Agreement (DTUA) signed by authorized official. Platform details: PhysioNet managed by MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology (NIBIB grant R01EB030362), Health Data Nexus alternative platform providing cloud compute. Distribution formats specify access tier per format (lines 587-609)
questions.quality_note: Exemplary access mechanism documentation. Two-tier system fully specified with distinct procedures for each tier. Platform URLs provided (PhysioNet, Health Data Nexus). Required forms enumerated (DUA, DARF, DTUA). Contact points given (DACO@b2ai-voice.org). Access requirements clearly distinguished by data sensitivity (featurized vs. raw audio). Institutional authorization requirements stated. Demonstrates complete transparency in access procedures.

questions.name: Reusability (License Clarity)
questions.description: License clearly defined with reuse terms
questions.evidence: License (lines 573-585): Named 'Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License', registered access via PhysioNet with signed DUA required. Permitted uses: 'commercial and non-commercial research use permitted for Authorized Researchers', 'Recipient encouraged to publish results in open-access journals'. Prohibited uses (lines 563-569): 'Sale of all or part of the data on any media is prohibited', 'Re-identification attempts are prohibited', use outside authorized research prohibited. Certificate of Confidentiality coverage explained (lines 576-578): 'must be asserted against compulsory legal demands'. Third-party restrictions (lines 620-627): 'Recipient shall not disclose, release, sell, rent, or lease data to third parties without prior written consent of Provider'. Retention policy (lines 662-674): two-year agreement term, destruction upon termination with 30-day certification, one copy retention for compliance allowed. No export controls. IP protections discouraged (lines 556-561): must respect Fort Lauderdale Agreement and Open Science principles
questions.quality_note: Exceptionally clear license with comprehensive reuse terms. Permitted uses explicitly stated (commercial and non-commercial research). Prohibited uses enumerated (sale, re-identification, unauthorized use). Legal protections explained (Certificate of Confidentiality). Sharing restrictions and retention policies detailed. Open science principles integrated. Balances data sharing for research with privacy protections. Demonstrates mature data governance framework.

strengths: Exceptional structural completeness with all mandatory fields populated at highest quality level (5/5 on all numeric questions in Category 1)
Outstanding keyword diversity (51 keywords) spanning clinical domains, technical tools, data standards, and ethical frameworks
Comprehensive ethical documentation including IRB approval, HIPAA Safe Harbor deidentification, Certificate of Confidentiality, and prospective consent processes
Exemplary access mechanism with fully documented two-tier system (registered access for featurized data, controlled access for raw audio) with clear procedures and contact points
Excellent standardization and interoperability with explicit BIDS v1.9.0 conformance and multiple standard formats (Parquet, TSV/JSON, WAV)
Detailed funding documentation with grant numbers, project timeline, and budget breakdown ($4.66M total funding)
Comprehensive version history with 5 versions documented, version-specific DOIs, and semi-annual release schedule
Exceptional collection protocol clarity with hardware specifications, all acoustic tasks enumerated, validated questionnaires named, and recruitment strategy detailed
Outstanding human subject representation with six detailed subpopulations, validation methods, and transparent limitations documented
Extensive cross-platform interlinking (10+ platforms) including PhysioNet, Health Data Nexus, GitHub, Zenodo, and NIH RePORTER
Clear license with comprehensive reuse terms balancing open science principles with privacy protections
Strong data integrity with structured version control, change logs, quality audit protocols, and processing provenance
weaknesses: Software tools documented without version numbers for most tools (b2aiprep, OpenSMILE, Praat, Parselmouth lack version specifics - only BIDS v1.9.0 versioned)

Limited associated publications (1 protocol paper, 1 data dictionary archive) - understandable given recent first release (late 2024) but would benefit from dataset descriptor paper and derivative research citations as they emerge
recommendations: Add specific version numbers for all preprocessing tools in software_and_tools section (e.g., 'OpenSMILE 3.0.0', 'Whisper large-v3', 'Parselmouth 0.4.3', 'b2aiprep v1.2.0'). Check GitHub releases or documentation for exact versions used.

Consider creating a comprehensive dataset descriptor paper for submission to a data journal (Scientific Data, GigaScience, Data in Brief) to complement the Interspeech 2024 protocol paper and increase citability
As derivative research publications using the dataset are published, add them to a 'citations' or 'references' section to demonstrate dataset impact and create bidirectional citation links
Document specific REDCap version and reproschema-ui version used in data collection workflow
Consider adding a 'software_versions' field or extending preprocessing_strategies entries to include exact version numbers and release dates for all tools in the processing pipeline
